title: Exact low-degree junta polynomial hypothesis
statement: Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $P\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ be a coordinate set, let $z$ assign signs on $P$, and let $\delta\in(0,1/2]$. For every batch of the specified restricted-sample size consisting of assignments on coordinates outside $P$ paired with signs, the polynomial hypothesis constructed from the batch evaluates exactly to the Boolean encoding of the restriction of $f$ under $z$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$P$ is a finite set of coordinates in $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$
the batch has the specified restricted-sample size and consists of free-coordinate assignments paired with signs
caveat: The polynomial-hypothesis construction and Boolean encoding of the restricted function are not defined in the supplied material.
